Using the minimal repro from lazy.nvim. Surround works.

        local map = function(keys, func, desc)
          vim.keymap.set("n", keys, func, { desc = desc })
        end
        --

        --  - va)  - [V]isually select [A]round [)]paren

        require("mini.ai").setup({
          n_lines = 128, -- text object search range
        })

        require("mini.files").setup({
          map("<leader>m", function()
            MiniFiles.open(MiniFiles.get_latest_path())
          end, "Open mini.files in parent directory"),
        })

        require("mini.indentscope").setup({
          draw = {
            animation = function()
              return 0
            end,
          },
        })

        require("mini.jump2d").setup({
          map("f", function()
            MiniJump2d.start(MiniJump2d.builtin_opts.single_character)
          end, "Mini.jump2d to specified character"),

        require("mini.pairs").setup()

        -- Add/delete/replace surroundings (brackets, quotes, etc.)

        require("mini.misc").setup()
        MiniMisc.setup_auto_root()

        --
      end,
    },
  },
})

reply_data.body:
> Please keep in mind that everything works, and has been doing so for many months, _except_ mini.surround. And until recently, mini.surround was working, too. But a couple of months ago I had some issues with plugin interactions and pinned mini.nvim, which-key, and one other plugin to a previous commit. A few days ago I un-pinned them to use current versions.

This sounds like an issue with 'which-key.nvim' rewrite about two months. I *think* 'timeoutlen' is the issue and [this should help](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/73f2e7a596bbb4e6ae6728d3a4426221ffc9512d/doc/mini-surround.txt#L570-L574). But here is a fuller list of steps I'd do to eliminate basic reasons:
- Execute `:=MiniSurround`. If it prints `nil`, then `require('mini.surround').setup()` was not called. Make sure it is called.
- Execute `:nmap s`. It should show a bunch of mappings from 'mini.surround'. If not, make sure there is no plugin interactive with those keymaps later.
- If both previous steps are resolved, make sure to have high enough 'timeoutlen' (by adding `vim.o.timeoutlen = 1000` in your config) and/or disable built-in `s` key (by adding `vim.keymap.set({ 'n', 'x' }, 's', '<Nop>')` line to your config). I personally use the second approach.
